'''Michael Howard Harris''' (born 1954) is an American mathematician known for his work in [[number theory]]. He is a professor of mathematics at [[Columbia University]] and professor emeritus of mathematics at [[Université Paris Cité]]. In 2025, he was elected to the [[American Philosophical Society]].<ref>https://www.amphilsoc.org/news/aps-elects-new-members-2025</ref>

==Early life and education==
Harris was born in [[Kingsessing, Philadelphia]], Pennsylvania<ref name="NAS"/> and is of Jewish descent.<ref>{{cite book |last1=Harris |first1=Michael |title=Mathematics without Apologies: Portrait of a Problematic Vocation |date=2015 |publisher=[[Princeton University Press]] |isbn=9780691154237 |page=373}}</ref> He received his B.A. in mathematics from [[Princeton University]] in 1973.<ref name="CV">{{cite web |last1=Harris |first1=Michael |title=CV |url=http://www.math.columbia.edu/~harris/website/cv |website=Michael Harris |access-date=July 24, 2023}}</ref> He received his M.A. and Ph.D. in mathematics from [[Harvard University]] under the supervision of [[Barry Mazur]] in 1976 and 1977 respectively.<ref name="CV"/><ref name="MathGenealogy">{{MathGenealogy |id=22503|name=Michael Harris }}</ref>

==Career==
Harris was a faculty member at [[Brandeis University]] from 1977 to 1994.<ref name="CV"/> In 1994, he became a professor of mathematics at [[Paris Diderot University]] and the [[Institut de mathématiques de Jussieu – Paris Rive Gauche]], where he has been emeritus since 2021.<ref name="CV"/><ref name="IMJ-PRG">{{cite web |title=Emérites |url=https://www.imj-prg.fr/emerites/ |website=Institut de mathématiques de Jussieu – Paris Rive Gauche |publisher=[[Institut de mathématiques de Jussieu – Paris Rive Gauche]] |access-date=June 24, 2023}}</ref> He became a professor of mathematics at [[Columbia University]] in 2013.<ref name="CV"/>

He was a member of the [[Institute for Advanced Study]] from 1983 to 1984 and in the fall of 2011.<ref>{{cite web |title=Michael Harris |url=https://www.ias.edu/scholars/michael-harris |website=Institute for Advanced Study |date=9 December 2019 |publisher=[[Institute for Advanced Study]] |access-date=June 24, 2023}}</ref> He has held visiting positions at various institutions, including [[Bethlehem University]], the [[Steklov Institute of Mathematics]], the [[Institut des Hautes Études Scientifiques]], [[Oxford University]], and the [[Mathematical Sciences Research Institute]].<ref name="CV"/>

His former doctoral students include [[Laurent Fargues]] and [[Gaëtan Chenevier]].<ref name="MathGenealogy"/>

He has organized or co-organized more than 20 conferences, workshops, and special programs in his field of number theory.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Michael Harris |url=https://www.helixcenter.org/participants/michael-harris/ |access-date=2025-01-28 |website=The Helix Center |language=en-US}}</ref> 

==Work==
===Research===
Harris's research focuses on [[arithmetic geometry]], [[automorphic forms]], [[L-function|''L''-function]]s, and [[Motive (algebraic geometry)|motives]].<ref name="AMS"/> He has developed the theory of [[coherent cohomology]] of [[Shimura variety|Shimura varieties]] and applied it to number theoretic problems on [[Special values of L-functions|special values of ''L''-functions]], [[Galois representations]], and the [[theta correspondence]].<ref name="NAS"/> His later work focuses on geometric aspects of the [[Langlands program]].<ref name="NAS"/>

In 2001, Harris and [[Richard Taylor (mathematician)|Richard Taylor]] proved the [[local Langlands conjecture]] for [[General linear group|GL(''n'')]] over a ''p''-adic [[local field]]

===''Mathematics without Apologies''===
Harris wrote the book ''Mathematics without Apologies: Portrait of a Problematic Vocation'', published in 2015.<ref>{{cite book | last=Harris | first=Michael | title=Mathematics without apologies : portrait of a problematic vocation | publisher=[[Princeton University Press]] | date=2015 | isbn=978-1-4008-5202-4 | oclc=900080550}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|author=McCleary, John|date=November 2018|url=https://www.ams.org/journals/notices/201810/rnoti-p1280.pdf|title=Review of ''Mathematics without Apologies: Portrait of a Problematic Vocation'' by Michael Harris|website=Notices of the AMS}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal|author=Alexander, Amir|author-link=Amir Alexander|title=Mathematics: Groping in the dark for glimpses of beauty (joint review of ''Birth of a Theorem'' by Cédric Villani and ''Mathematics without Apologies'' by Michael Harris)|journal=Nature|volume=519|issue=7541|pages=31–32|date=4 March 2015|doi=10.1038/519031a|doi-access=free}} (See [[Cédric Villani]].)</ref><ref>{{cite web|author=Hunacek, Michael|date=August 4, 2015|title=review of ''Mathematics without Apologies''|website=MAA Reviews|url=https://www.maa.org/press/maa-reviews/mathematics-without-apologies-portrait-of-a-problematic-vocation}}</ref>

===''Silicon Reckoner''===
Since 2021, Harris has written the newsletter ''Silicon Reckoner'' exploring questions and issues related to the mechanization of mathematics and [[artificial intelligence]].<ref>{{cite web|author=Harris, Michael|title=About Silicon Reckoner|url=https://siliconreckoner.substack.com/about}}</ref>

==Recognition==
Harris received the [[Sophie Germain Prize]] (2006),<ref name="CV"/> the [[Clay Research Award]] (joint with Richard Taylor, 2007),<ref name="NAS"/><ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.gap-system.org/~history/Societies/Clay.html |title=Clay Award |access-date=2011-06-01 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120316162039/http://www.gap-system.org/~history/Societies/Clay.html |archive-date=2012-03-16 }}</ref> the Grand Prix Scientifique de la [[Simone and Cino Del Duca Foundation|Fondation Simone et Cino del Duca]] (2009),<ref name="CV"/> He is a two-time invited speaker at the [[International Congress of Mathematicians]] (2002, 2014).<ref name="CV"/>

Harris was a [[Sloan Research Fellowship|Sloan Research Fellow]] (1983–1985) and a member of the [[Institut Universitaire de France]] (2001–2011)<ref name="CV"/><ref name="NAS"/> He has been elected a [[Member of the Academia Europaea]] (2016),<ref name="CV"/> [[Fellow of the American Mathematical Society]] (2019),<ref name="CV"/><ref name="AMS">{{cite web|url=https://www.ams.org/fellows_by_year.cgi?year=2019 |title=2019 Class of the Fellows of the AMS |website=American Mathematical Society |publisher=[[American Mathematical Society]]|access-date=June 24, 2023}}</ref> Member of the [[American Academy of Arts and Sciences]] (2019),<ref name="CV"/> and Member of the [[National Academy of Sciences]] (2022).<ref name="NAS">{{cite web |title=Michael Harris |url=https://www.nasonline.org/directory-entry/michael-harris-rqqsrr/ |website=National Academy of Sciences |publisher=[[National Academy of Sciences]] |access-date=June 24, 2023}}</ref><ref name="CV"/>
